extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent attorneys/agents, and applicants preparing or prosecuting PCT international applications (ISA/IPEA and national-stage practitioners)
extracted.subtask_short: PCT unity and sequence listing rules
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for meeting PCT/USPTO requirements on nucleotide/amino-acid sequence listings and on the requirement of unity of invention (including procedures for lack of unity, additional fees, protests, and special situations such as Markush and intermediate/final products).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence identifier format
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequences included in the sequence listing shall be referred to by the sequence identifier preceded by 'SEQ ID NO:', even if the sequence is also embedded in the description, claims or drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always use the exact 'SEQ ID NO:' prefix when referring to sequences throughout the application (description, claims, drawings) to ensure consistent identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing must comply with Administrative Instructions / Annex C (WIPO ST.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an international application filed under the PCT contains a disclosure of nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences that are required to be listed within a sequence listing, PCT Rule 5.2 requires that the description shall include a sequence listing part of the description complying with the standard provided for in the Administrative Instructions; any sequence listing shall comply with Annex C of the Administrative Instructions (WIPO Standard ST.26).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence listings should follow the WIPO ST.26 formatting and content standards (see MPEP §2412-2419, especially §2414.05). WIPO ST.26 resources are available from WIPO's standards pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisability to submit ST.26 XML at international filing
rubrics_metrics.description: It is advisable for the applicant to submit a sequence listing compliant with WIPO Standard ST.26 XML format together with the international application on the international filing date rather than to wait for an invitation by the ISA or IPEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early submission avoids late-furnishing procedures and potential limits to search/examination if the ISA/IPEA must proceed without a compliant listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISA/IPEA invitation to furnish sequence listing when noncompliant or absent
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant has not provided a sequence listing in accordance with Annex C and the USPTO acts as ISA or IPEA, the ISA/IPEA may invite applicant to furnish a sequence listing with a late furnishing fee under PCT Rule 13ter; this invitation will specify a time limit for a proper response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An invitation will set a deadline; if applicant does not comply timely, the ISA/IPEA may limit search/examination to what is meaningful without the listing (see PCT Rule 13ter and MPEP references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper response to invitation to furnish sequence listing
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper response includes submission of a sequence listing in accordance with Annex C of the Administrative Instructions, payment of the late furnishing fee specified in 37 CFR 1.445(a)(5), and a statement that the sequence listing does not go beyond the disclosure of the international application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the statement affirms no added matter; include the compliant listing and fee within the invited time limit to have the listing considered for search/examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of not furnishing required sequence listing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a sequence listing compliant with WIPO ST.26 has not been furnished to the ISA/IPEA within the time limit set in the invitation, the ISA/IPEA will only search/examine the international application to the extent that a meaningful search/examination can be performed without the sequence listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely provide a compliant listing can materially limit the scope of international search and examination; consider early compliance to avoid incomplete searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of WIPO ST.25 for older filings
rubrics_metrics.description: For international applications having an international filing date before July 1, 2022 (editor's note), sequence listings must comply with WIPO Standard ST.25 (the standard specified in Annex C of the Administrative Instructions then in force).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the applicable standard based on filing date (ST.25 before July 1, 2022 vs ST.26 thereafter) and consult the correct Administrative Instructions / historical Annex C and MPEP §1823.02 subsection II as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of unity of invention (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application shall relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions so linked as to form a single general inventive concept ('requirement of unity of invention'). (PCT Rule 13.1)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity is a threshold requirement checked by the ISA and may impact national/regional phases; claims should be drafted and organized with a single general inventive concept in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: When unity is fulfilled (technical relationship / special technical features)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity exists where a group of inventions claimed in one international application have a technical relationship involving one or more of the same or corresponding 'special technical features.' (PCT Rule 13.2)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether claimed inventions share one or more technical features that define the contribution over the prior art; this is the basis for unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'special technical features'
rubrics_metrics.description: The expression 'special technical features' means those technical features that define a contribution which each of the claimed inventions, considered as a whole, makes over the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate candidate features for whether they provide a shared contribution over prior art (novelty and inventive step considerations are relevant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of unity not affected by manner of claiming
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination whether a group of inventions is so linked as to form a single general inventive concept shall be made without regard to whether the inventions are claimed in separate claims or as alternatives within a single claim. (PCT Rule 13.3)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity analysis looks to substance, not claim drafting form; alternatives within one claim can still present lack of unity if they are distinct embodiments without a unifying inventive concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claims permitted despite potentially being separate inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is permitted to include in the same international application a reasonable number of dependent claims claiming specific forms of the invention claimed in an independent claim, even where the features of any dependent claim could be considered as constituting in themselves an invention. (PCT Rule 13.4)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dependent claims that add specific features may be retained with the independent claim if the independent claim itself satisfies unity; the presence of potentially patentable dependent claims does not by itself create lack of unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model option for designated States
rubrics_metrics.description: Any designated State in which the grant of a utility model is sought on the basis of an international application may apply its national law concerning utility models instead of PCT Rules 13.1–13.4, provided the applicant has at least two months from the expiration of the Article 22 time limit to adapt the application. (PCT Rule 13.5)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that some designated States may apply different national utility-model rules; time allowances are mandated for adaptation.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT Rule 40 — Invitation to pay additional fees must state reasons/time/amount/protest fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The invitation to pay additional fees (Article 17(3)(a)) shall (i) specify the reasons for which the application is not considered as complying with unity, (ii) invite the applicant to pay additional fees within one month and indicate the amount, and (iii) invite payment of any protest fee within one month and indicate that amount. (PCT Rule 40.1)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invitations must be specific and set a one-month time limit for fee payment and any protest fee; track deadlines carefully to preserve rights to protest or pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional fees: determination and payment to ISA
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of additional fees due for searching under Article 17(3)(a) shall be determined by the competent International Searching Authority and shall be payable direct to the ISA. (PCT Rule 40.2(a)–(b))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect fee calculation and collection from the ISA; confirm applicable rates and payment instructions from the ISA issuing the invitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment under protest and review procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may pay additional fees under protest, accompanied by a reasoned statement that the application complies with unity or that the additional fees are excessive; such protests are examined by a review body within the ISA, which may order total or partial reimbursement if protest justified. The protest and decision may be notified to designated Offices and translations filed. A protest fee may be required; if unpaid the protest is considered not made. Protest fee refunded if protest entirely justified. (PCT Rule 40.2(c)–(e))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When paying under protest, provide a reasoned statement and be prepared to seek review; note the procedural requirement for translations and possible protest fee and refund rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR combinations of categories that confer unity
rubrics_metrics.description: An international or national-stage application containing claims to different categories will be considered to have unity if the claims are drawn to one of the following combinations: (1) product and process specially adapted for the manufacture of said product; (2) product and process of use of said product; (3) product, process specially adapted for manufacture, and use; (4) process and apparatus/means specifically designed for carrying out the process; (5) product, process specially adapted for manufacture, and apparatus/means for carrying out the process. (37 CFR 1.475(b))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific category-combination permutations are treated as having unity provided the required relationships (e.g., 'specially adapted', 'specifically designed') exist in the claimed subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity determination: a priori vs a posteriori and practical approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of unity may be evident a priori (before considering prior art) or a posteriori (after considering prior art). Examiners should avoid raising or maintaining lack of unity on a narrow, literal, or academic approach and should apply a broad, practical assessment of interdependence in relation to the state of the art, giving the benefit of any doubt to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use practical analysis rather than overly technical/legalistic parsing; consider examples (e.g., independent claims to A+X, A+Y, X+Y lack unity a priori; A+X and A+Y have unity a priori unless A is shown to be known in which case lack of unity may arise a posteriori).

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on independent claims for unity; role of dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity of invention is to be considered primarily in relation to independent claims. If independent claims avoid the prior art and satisfy unity, dependent claims present no unity problem even if they include further inventions. If an independent claim does not avoid the prior art, a posteriori lack of unity may be raised and the link among dependent claims must be considered carefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First assess independent claims interpreted in light of the description/drawings; dependent claims only raise unity issues if the independent claims fail to avoid the prior art or leave no unifying inventive concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus/species and combination/subcombination guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Genus claims that avoid the prior art are acceptable provided the genus is directed only to alternatives of a similar nature; combination/subcombination situations similarly cause no objection if subcombination claim avoids prior art and the combination claim includes all features of the subcombination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To determine 'similar nature' for genus/species situations, apply the Markush / subsection III.B principles; examine whether alternatives are of similar technical character and share the unifying features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush practice criteria (alternatives of similar nature)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Markush groupings (single claim defining alternatives), the requirement of technical interrelationship and same/corresponding special technical features is met when the alternatives are of a similar nature. For chemical compounds, this is satisfied when (A) all alternatives have a common property or activity, and (B) either (1) a significant structural element is shared by all alternatives or (2) all alternatives belong to a recognized class of chemical compounds in the art. (subsection III.B)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess common property/activity and whether a common structural element is structurally significant given prior art, or whether members belong to a recognized class with expected similar behavior. If at least one Markush alternative is not novel, unity should be reconsidered by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediate and final product unity criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity shall be considered present for intermediate and final products where (A) the intermediate and final products have the same essential structural element (basic chemical structures same or technically closely interrelated with intermediate incorporating an essential structural element into final product), and (B) the intermediate and final products are technically interrelated (final product manufactured directly from intermediate or separated by a small number of intermediates all containing the same essential structural element).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity may be recognized even if some structures are unknown provided there is sufficient evidence of technical interrelation; multiple intermediate variants are acceptable only if they share the same essential structural element relevant to the final product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of searching additional inventions without payment when minimal effort
rubrics_metrics.description: If little or no additional search effort is required, for reasons of economy the examiner may search, while searching the main invention, one or more additional inventions without payment of additional fees; the international search for such additional inventions will then have to be completed in further classification units when additional search fees have been paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may opportunistically search related inventions if this saves resources; applicants should note that final search coverage for additional inventions may depend on payment of any required additional search fees.
